questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Ghana?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: Thirty-one million people live there; its capital was once Cape Coast, but now it is Accra.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Ghana about 238,535 square kilometres; Benin about 114,763 square kilometres; Togo about 56,785 square kilometres; Guinea-Bissau about 36,125 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Ghana?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Ghana on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Ghana article.

questions.proof: The hilly Akuapim-Togo ranges are found along the country's eastern border.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Ghana on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Ghana on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Accra?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Ghana is Accra.
